elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens "On expiry or termination of this Agreement or an Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall ...", so the obligations trigger on both expiry and any termination.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "at Customer's request provide transition assistance for up to six months".

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty days return all Customer Data", governed by the opening temporal anchor "On expiry or termination of this Agreement or an Order Form", so the 30 days runs from expiry/termination rather than from a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "return all Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "after that return, delete Customer Data from its systems and certify the deletion in writing" — deletion sequenced after return and certification is express.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same opening trigger: "On expiry or termination of this Agreement or an Order Form for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Assistance available "for up to six months", which exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return of all Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within thirty days of expiry or termination.

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as missing: Section 10.1-10.2 addresses only access wind-down, Deliverable delivery and Fee refunds, and Section 16.5 covers Confidential Information while deferring Customer Data elsewhere, so no transition-assistance or data-return obligation existed.

All six preferred elements are carried by the single inserted paragraph in operative language, so the preferred level is position-complete; the fallback thresholds (90 days assistance, 30-day export) are also satisfied a fortiori.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion in the termination section, no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no added damages categories or procedural machinery, and existing favourable language in 10.1, 10.2 and 16.5 is retained unchanged.

Non-blocking drafting notes: the inserted paragraph carries no section number in the rendered text although the rationale calls it Section 10.3 — number it for citability; and Section 16.5's retained sentence "Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15" could be read as excluding the new clause, so consider adding the new section number to that cross-reference. Neither defect leaves an undefined term or dangling reference, so intent is preserved.
